block_05_direct_answer.title: Direct answer
block_05_direct_answer.body_html: Buying off-plan can make sense when the project quality, price and buyer timeline justify the construction risk. For a Dubai purchase, check developer strength, escrow and registration where relevant, payment plan, project progress, handover terms and comparable ready alternatives. It is less suitable when immediate use, financing certainty or a finished property is more important.

items.answer: Buying off-plan can make sense when the project quality, price and buyer timeline justify the construction risk. For a Dubai purchase, review delivery evidence, current project status and material documentation before relying on the quality of the launch or sales presentation.
items.question: Should I buy off-plan property?

items.answer: Off-plan and ready property solve different buyer needs, so neither is universally better. Model deposits, instalments, financing and completion payments for both routes instead of comparing only the initial purchase price.
items.question: How do I compare off-plan and ready property?

items.answer: Off-plan and ready property offer different trade-offs rather than a universally better choice. Account for construction, delivery and specification risk in off-plan while checking condition, refurbishment and existing-building risks in ready property.
items.question: How do off-plan and ready property compare?

items.answer: Neither off-plan nor ready property is automatically better for every buyer. Consider assignment rules, mortgage options, resale liquidity and tenant demand before deciding which purchase format offers the stronger practical route.
